Lakers Nation > Blog > Lakers News > Walker Kessler ‘Excited To Compete’ In First Game Against Utah Jazz Lakers News Walker Kessler ‘Excited To Compete’ In First Game Against Utah Jazz
 Matthew Moreno Published: 10/25/2026 3 Min Read Oct 16, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Lakers center Walker Kessler (14) during pregame warmups before a against the Denver Nuggets at Crypto.com Arena. Mandatory Credit: Jon Endow-Imagn Images SHARE Walker Kessler is off to a terrific start with the Los Angeles Lakers and next is what figures to be a hostile environment on Sunday.
 The Lakers’ first road game of the season is against the Utah Jazz, who traded Kessler to the Lakers during the offseason. Utah received unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033, and first-round swaps in 2028 and 2030 as part of the sign-and-trade.
 Kessler has spoken fondly of his time in the Jazz organization, and reiterated that sentiment when looking ahead to his return to the Delta Center.
 “I’m so excited to compete against those guys,” Kessler said. “Coach (Will) Hardy does a great job with that franchise and all my past teammates, they’re great players. Really talented, really competitive. So I think it’s going to be a very competitive game. 
 “But I’m just excited to go compete.”
 Kessler is heading into the matchup with the Jazz on the heels of back-to-back games with at least 20 points for the first time in his career. The 25-year-old scored 26 points on a perfect 12-for-12 shooting night in his Lakers debut and followed it up with 22 points agains the Los Angeles Clippers.
 Kessler’s performance in his first game with the Lakers prompted Shaquille O’Neal to declare him the best big man in the NBA.
 Although the 25-year-old is looking forward to facing his former Jazz teammates, the fan reception may not be that welcoming. Kessler and the Jazz front office reportedly were at odds during his final season with the team due to contractual matters. 
 Why did the Jazz trade Walker Kessler?
 The Jazz somewhat surprisingly decided to trade Kessler, a restricted free agent at the time, because of the significant return they received from the Lakers. Prior to that, the Jazz reportedly offered him a five-year, $140 million contract that Kessler rejected.
 He wound up receiving a four-year, $130 million deal with the Lakers in the sign-and-trade.
 Kessler was drafted by Memphis Grizzlies with the 22nd overall pick in 2022, but his rights were sent to the Minnesota Timberwolves. Kessler then was traded by the Timberwolves to the Jazz as part of the Rudy Gobert deal. 
 He played four seasons in Utah, though was limited to just five games last year because of a right shoulder injury that required surgery.
